steps.body: Remember walking the fence — tracing every side and adding the distances? That has a formula name too: **PERIMETER = 2 × (length + width).** For a 6-by-4 rectangle: 2×(6+4)=2×10=**20.** Two lengths, two widths, walked all the way around.

widget.prompt: Match each rectangle's dimensions to its perimeter.
widget.missFeedback: Add length and width, then double the sum — walking all four sides.
widget.successFeedback: 2×(6+4)=20, 2×(9+5)=28, 2×(7+3)=20 — different-shaped rectangles can share a perimeter.

predict.prompt: Which is the longer walk around: a 1-by-9 rectangle or a 5-by-5?
predict.reveal: Both fences total 20 — perimeter listens only to the sum of the sides, not to how skinny or square the shape looks.

explanationVariants: Add the two sides, then double for all four.

widget.prompt: A rectangle is 15 units by 9 units. What is its perimeter?

commonErrors.feedback: 135 multiplies the sides — that finds the AREA, not the perimeter. Walking around: 2×(15+9)=48.
24 is only 15+9, one trip around half the rectangle. Double it for all four sides: 2×24=48.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Add the two sides, then multiply by 2.

steps.body: Area and perimeter move **independently.** A 3-by-8 rectangle and a 5-by-6 rectangle both have perimeter 22 — but their areas are 24 and 30. Same fence length, different amount of grass inside. One never tells you the other.

explanationVariants: 3×8 gives perimeter 2×(3+8)=22 and area 3×8=24. 5×6 gives perimeter 2×(5+6)=22 and area 5×6=30 — same perimeter, bigger area.
Matching fence lengths can enclose very different amounts of space.

widget.prompt: A 3-by-8 rectangle and a 5-by-6 rectangle both have a perimeter of 22. Do they have the same area?

options.label: No — 3×8=24 but 5×6=30
options.feedback: Same perimeter doesn't guarantee the same area. 24 and 30 are different amounts of surface.

options.label: Yes — same perimeter always means same area
options.feedback: Perimeter and area move independently. Here, 3×8=24 and 5×6=30 — different areas despite matching perimeters.

options.label: Yes, because both numbers add to the same total
options.feedback: Adding to the same total (perimeter) doesn't multiply to the same product (area). 24 ≠ 30.

options.label: Can't tell without drawing them
options.feedback: The formulas settle it directly: 3×8=24 and 5×6=30 — no drawing needed.

widget.prompt: Sort each rectangle pair by what they share.

items.label: 3×8 and 5×6
items.feedback: Both have perimeter 22, but areas 24 and 30 differ.

items.label: 2×12 and 4×6
items.feedback: Both have area 24, but perimeters 28 and 20 differ.

items.label: 1×20 and 4×5
items.feedback: Both have area 20, but perimeters 42 and 18 differ.

items.label: 1×9 and 4×6
items.feedback: Both have perimeter 20, but areas 9 and 24 differ.

widget.missFeedback: Compute both the perimeter and the area for each pair, then compare.
widget.successFeedback: Every pair here matches on one measure while differing sharply on the other.

explanationVariants: Half the perimeter (13) minus the known side (7) gives the missing side.

widget.prompt: A rectangle has a perimeter of 26 units. One side is 7 units. What is the other side?

commonErrors.feedback: 19 subtracts 7 from the FULL perimeter (26), but perimeter counts each side TWICE. Halve 26 to 13 first, then subtract 7: 6.
12 divides 26 by 2 but forgets to subtract the known side. Half the perimeter is 13; 13−7=6.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Half the perimeter (26÷2=13) is length+width; subtract the known side (7).

hints: Fencing goes AROUND the yard — that's perimeter, not area.
Double that sum for all four sides.
explanationVariants: A 15-by-9 yard needs 2×(15+9)=2×24=48 units of fencing.
Fencing traces the perimeter, not the surface.

widget.prompt: A rectangular yard is 15 feet by 9 feet. How many feet of fencing are needed to go all the way around it?

commonErrors.feedback: 135 multiplies the sides — that's the AREA (the grass inside), not the fence length. Fencing needs perimeter: 2×(15+9)=48.
24 is only 15+9, half the trip around. Double it for all four sides: 2×24=48.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Fencing needs perimeter: add the two sides, then double.

takeaways: Perimeter = 2 × (length + width) — walking every side, formalized.
Area and perimeter move independently — matching one never guarantees matching the other.
Perimeter answers 'how much distance around,' like fencing or framing.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Perimeter = 2 × (length + width).** For a 5-by-2 rectangle: 5+2=7, then 2×7=14 — walking all four sides.

widget.prompt: A rectangle is 5 units by 2 units. What is its perimeter?

options.feedback: 10 multiplies the sides — that's area. Perimeter is 2×(5+2)=14.
7 is only one trip halfway around. Double it: 2×7=14.
